summary: This bill amends 31 U.S.C. 5336(b)(1)(B) to require companies formed or registered before January 1, 2024, to file beneficial ownership information reports by January 1, 2026, rather than within two years after the regulations take effect.

scores.thoughts: The bill modifies a regulatory filing deadline under the Corporate Transparency Act but does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures. It has no bearing on spending levels.
The legislation addresses only the timing of beneficial ownership information reports and contains no tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures.
No provisions relate to health coverage, insurance markets, or medical regulation.
The bill does not address firearms, background checks, or gun ownership regulations.
No immigration, border, or visa-related content appears in the text.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense appropriations, military policy, or national security spending provisions are present.
The legislation does not engage with environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are mentioned or altered.
The bill has no connection to schools, student aid, or education policy.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions exist.

While the underlying Corporate Transparency Act supports anti-money-laundering efforts, this bill merely adjusts an existing filing deadline and does not alter sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.
No tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export regulations are addressed.
The bill does not affect deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation contains no foreign assistance or international aid measures.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance content is present.
The bill adjusts a federal data-reporting deadline but does not change privacy standards, data-protection rules, or technology regulation.
No labor, union, or workplace rights provisions appear.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
